# yqr

> yqr is a jq-style query and editing tool for YAML, written in Rust. Reads are byte-preserving by default: nodes you do not touch are emitted as their original bytes, so comments, quoting, indentation and line endings survive. The write tier changes only the bytes the filter targets, or refuses.

Install: cargo install yqr
Invoke:  yqr [-r] [-i] [-N] '<filter>' [file]      (stdin when file is omitted)
         yqr validate [--strict] <file>...

Flags:
  -r, --raw-output   print a string's value, not its YAML quoting
  -i, --in-place     write the edit back to the file (mutating filters only)
  -N, --normalize    re-serialize instead of preserving bytes

Exit codes:
  0  success
  1  validate found a problem in the file
  3  the filter could not be lexed or parsed
  5  runtime or I/O error, including a refused edit

Source:    https://github.com/zoosky/yqr
Package:   https://crates.io/crates/yqr

## yqr guide

- [Byte-for-byte YAML editing, explained](/yqr/guide/fidelity): Why `yqr '.' f` reproduces `f` exactly, what survives a read, and when you want `--normalize` instead.
- [Editing Kubernetes manifests without reformatting them](/yqr/guide/kubernetes): How to bump an image tag or a replica count so the diff is one line, and which edits yqr refuses outright.
- [Enumerating a mapping without losing the keys](/yqr/guide/enumerate): How to report what each entry of a mapping is about, with `to_entries`, when iterating throws the keys away.
- [Validating YAML from the command line](/yqr/guide/validate): How to check a file is still correct after an edit, what each exit code means, and how duplicate keys are reported.

## How yqr compares to other YAML tools

- [yqr and yq -- what actually changes in your file](/yqr/compare/yq): What yq and yqr each do to your file's formatting, on a read and on an edit, measured side by side.

## yqr demo

- [yqr demo](/yqr/demo): A runnable script that walks yqr's query and edit surface against sample files you can inspect afterwards.
